correctness.rationale: The Fourier-mode characteristic roots cross the imaginary axis only when d_q=0; the stable side has d_q>0. Three explicit Itô covariance identities yield E|g_hat|^2=C/d_q and E|y_hat|^2=C[1+(1+cos q)/(2T^2 d_q)]. Parseval yields exact N=3 energy and derivative sigma^2(gamma T-1)/(12 gamma T^2 d^2). A standalone independent 25-equation exact-rational Lyapunov solver verified ten stable cases and the rational increasing-energy witness. The theorem explicitly excludes unstable and collision-free claims.

value.rationale: The fluctuation Hamiltonian is explicitly used in the originating traffic model to judge suppression of traffic noise. The theorem proves a sharp complete response trichotomy for the minimal admissible ring: increasing stiffness always lowers speed and headway variances, yet can raise mean Hamiltonian fluctuation energy, with exact neutral boundary gamma T=1. General Fourier derivatives reveal mode-dependent mechanisms and provide a meaningful limit to interpreting simulated monotonic energy reduction. The natural invariant and parameters are fixed by the model, not arbitrary finite sampling.
